claims.text: A spectral module already exists and this one does NOT replace or fork it.
claims.why: Reference to structcore.topology.spectral_partition; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: structcore.topology.spectral_partition produces ONE PRODUCT: a two-way visualization cut of the structcore index graph, served to the web UI at /api/topology.
claims.why: structcore.topology.spectral_partition not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: This module produces NO partition and serves no UI. It produces MEASUREMENTS ABOUT A PARTITION WE ALREADY DECLARED (the package layout on disk), over the reachability graph from daedalus.mapping.reach.analyse
claims.why: The module imports declared_package from inventory and defines graph_from_reach which adapts reach.analyse output; no partition or UI code present.

claims.text: the same graph docs/architecture-state.json is built from, which is branch-aware and deliberately refuses the if False: and swallowed-ImportError edges the structcore index carries (see reach.analyse's docstring).
claims.why: References reach.analyse docstring and architecture-state.json; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Different graph, different output, different consumer. The Fiedler vector shows up in both because both need the second Laplacian eigenvector; in neither case is an eigensolver hand-rolled -- both call networkx/scipy.
claims.why: No eigensolver implementation in this chunk; relies on networkx/scipy via HAVE_MATH guard.

claims.text: If you are adding a fifth spectral thing, extend one of these two rather than opening a third.
claims.why: Refers to two existing spectral modules; only this one is shown.

claims.text: NO GRAPH IS BUILT HERE. There is exactly one import-graph extractor on the mapping side and it is reach.analyse. graph_from_reach is an adapter over its output, not a second walker.
claims.why: graph_from_reach accepts a report parameter and returns nx.Graph; no graph extraction logic present.

claims.text: Nothing here returns an exit code, blocks a lane, moves a picker band, or decides anything. Every value is a measurement attached to a candidate a human or the picker already had for other reasons.
claims.why: No exit codes, blocking, or decision logic in this chunk; only data structures and adapters.

claims.text: There is no threshold constant in this file on purpose.
claims.why: No threshold constants defined; only DEFAULT_TRIALS, DEFAULT_SEED, DEFAULT_K_MAX which are parameters, not thresholds.

claims.text: Undirected on purpose: Laplacian spectral theory as used here (Fiedler vector, algebraic connectivity, modularity, conductance) is defined for undirected graphs. A imports B is projected to an undirected edge, which loses direction and keeps adjacency. That trade is stated in every report dict as graph_type so no reader mistakes a cut for a dependency direction.
claims.why: graph_from_edges creates an undirected nx.Graph; graph_from_reach is expected to do the same (not fully shown).

claims.text: Importing beats restating a rule that must stay identical across the two modules or the numbers stop being comparable.
claims.why: declared_package is imported from .inventory, not redefined.

claims.text: mirrors structcore.topology's guard, deliberately: same extra, same word
claims.why: structcore.topology not present in this chunk; guard structure matches typical pattern.

claims.text: Exists so a synthetic graph with known ground truth can be measured by the exact code path the repo graph goes through. A metric validated on a different code path than the one that ships is not validated.
claims.why: graph_from_edges is a standalone function that constructs nx.Graph; it can be used for testing with synthetic data.

claims.text: a self-import is not a structural edge
claims.why: Code explicitly skips edges where target == source.
